findings.evidence: user prompt: 'the right approach for compass calibration'; I3 lists FP-rate-target / friction-budget / Watkins-compliance as open questions; pred4 explicitly verifiable: false
findings.rationale: Rule 2 — evidence asymmetry. The intent has no falsifiable target. 'Right' is a normative word doing the work a measurable threshold should be doing.
findings.summary: 'The right approach' is aspirational, not a checkable success criterion

findings.evidence: I1 enumerates four candidate referents (threshold / weight table / whole heuristic / LLM rewrite); I4 repeats the same ambiguity at v1.1-scope level
findings.rationale: Rule 4 — universality vs instances. Different determinism profiles (pred1), different test-break risk (pred2), different token-cost profiles (pred3). Treating 'calibration' as one issue lets the answer to the easiest instance masquerade as the answer to the general problem.
findings.summary: 'Calibration' collapses four distinct problems into one word

findings.evidence: I2 lists three candidate inputs as open questions; no predicate asserts any of them is collected, schema'd, or queryable
findings.rationale: A calibration plan whose inputs are themselves unspecified isn't a plan, it's a wish.
findings.summary: Input signals (I2) are ungrounded — no evidence the bypass-log frequency, labels, or feedback channels exist in measurable form

critique.narrative: The intent is honest about what it doesn't know but 'brainstorm the right approach' is not yet a reviewable intent, it's a pre-intent. Recommend: iterate by forcing I1 to a single referent and I3 to a single metric.

findings.rationale: Calibration by definition tunes parameters of an existing mechanism. Replacing the heuristic with an LLM is not calibration, it is replacement, and conflicts directly with pred3 (token-free at trigger time).
findings.summary: I4 Position-3 (heuristic rewrite to LLM-based) is undeclared scope expansion masquerading as an option

findings.evidence: pred4: 'change must reduce FP rate below baseline by some unspecified amount'
findings.rationale: Per Rule 1, conflates aspirational success criteria with declared facts.
findings.summary: pred4 invents a quantitative FP-reduction target the user never specified

findings.evidence: I2: 'bypass-log frequency? labeled prompts? user feedback?'
findings.rationale: Premature abstraction: pre-commits to a multi-signal calibration framework when zero are wired up.
findings.summary: I2 enumerates three signal sources before any one is shown to be needed

critique.narrative: The decomposition is doing the user's thinking for them in a direction the user did not authorize. Collapse to I1+I3+I4-Position-1/2 only and ask the user to confirm scope.

findings.evidence: pred4 ('reduce FP rate below baseline') + I4 (scope includes 'full keyword/weight table rebuild' or 'heuristic rewrite to LLM-based')
findings.rationale: Predicates only constrain false-positive direction. Compass was deliberately built token-free, so there is no trace of a non-fire. Asymmetric observability + asymmetric predicate coverage = unrecoverable drift. The 'data-loss' analog is loss of guardrail coverage: prompts that should have been intercepted reach the model and produce irreversible downstream effects.
findings.summary: No rollback path for a calibration that silently shifts FN rate even if FP drops as required

findings.evidence: I4 ('heuristic rewrite to LLM-based') vs pred1 ('deterministic') and pred3 ('token-free at trigger time')
findings.rationale: Any LLM-at-trigger-time calibration violates pred3 unconditionally and almost certainly pred1. The decomposition should have rejected I4's LLM branch a priori.
findings.summary: I4's 'heuristic rewrite to LLM-based' option directly violates pred1 and pred3 and is not eliminated by the decomposition

findings.evidence: I2 ('bypass-log frequency? labeled prompts? user feedback?')
findings.rationale: Prompt distribution shifts will silently invalidate the calibration with no trigger to re-run.
findings.summary: I2 input signals omit drift / distribution-shift detection; calibration is treated as one-shot

critique.narrative: The decomposition's most dangerous asymmetry is that pred4 only constrains false positives while compass's token-free design makes false negatives invisible. A calibration can satisfy every stated predicate and still degrade the system in a way the system itself cannot report. Recommend iterate: add a paired FN benchmark or shadow-fire log.
